name: 1812 Prairie Avenue — George H. Wheeler house (Burnham & Root, 1884), a stone and brick front under a shaped Flemish gable

grade.why: Pictured: 2 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: Built for George H. Wheeler on the Real Estate and Building Journal's permit of June 7, 1884 ('3-story dwelling, 30x80', the Prairie library's npo-1812-rebj-1884-06-07-wheeler-dwelling-permit), photographed by Albert Levy c. 1885-1900 and drawn on the 1911 sheet ('3B'); the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). The range claims the 1904 target and the sheet's date and no more.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the K01 main body at its south (low-v) side, on the 1911 sheet's traced main part (s28fp-1812-b1) through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the draft's origin moved 9.82 m toward the street and 2.25 m south along its own frame (T-2543), to where the trace's south strip begins (sheet-local x 1370.0, y -3260.25). The georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation -0.616 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1812 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1812 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

footprint.note: The main body: the trace's front 15.1 m from the street wall (sheet-local x 1385.1) back to where its south strip begins (x 1370.0), and the full 8.5 m width the trace draws from the south wall (y -3260.25) to 0.13 m short of 1808's south wall (y -3251.63 on the trace), so the two never touch. The permit's '30x80' (9.1 m by 24.4 m) is the same house in round feet. The 1.6 m deeper part of the trace behind it is the rear range (rear_wings).

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: 3 full storeys, which the photograph shows over its raised basement, and the 1884 permit's '3-story dwelling'.

construction.note: The sheet colours the building brick; the photograph shows a stone basement and a stone-faced first storey under brick upper storeys banded and dressed in stone. T-2914: the street front is built so, its K02 stone stopping at the second floor's belt and the K03 brick over it, and the south projection's wall brick over its rock-faced basement; the sides and rear are brick.

principal_floor_m.note: Read through the photograph's camera (data/reference_views/wheeler_house_1812_prairie/levy_front.json): the entrance landing stands 148 px over the walk at the front's 88.5 px a metre, 1.67 m, and the stair rises to it in about seven risers; built at 1.65 m.

storey_heights_m.note: Floor to floor at the front's plane, through the photograph's camera: the belt over the first storey stands at about 5.6 m over the walk, the projection's top (the balcony's floor) at 9.45 m, and the third storey's two arched windows rise to crowns at about 12.2 m, over the gable's kneelers (11.6 m): the wall head is set just over them, at 12.45 m. The third storey's wall head is K01's eave; the gable stands on it (shaped_gable).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone-faced street wall of a three-storey house: 18 inches, as K01's other stone fronts (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

service_wall_brick.note: The sides and rear in K03's common brick, laid in common bond, as the row's other K01 houses (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

stone_front.note: The photograph shows the basement in rock-faced stone to a smooth water table at the principal floor, the entrance bay's first storey in coursed smooth stone up to the second-floor belt, and every wall over that belt in brick, banded and dressed in stone (quoined jambs, sills, lintels, voussoirs); its monochrome does not say which stone. Built in K02's brown sandstone, rock-faced, over two rusticated base courses (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543). T-2914: the stone stops at the second floor's line (brick_above_m 5.6 m, the top of the belt under the second storey) and the street front over it is the K03 brick, its belts, sills, flat arches, voussoirs and the north window's quoined surround still stone. The first storey's coursing is the kit's equal courses where the print shows an ashlar beside the porch arch (L-k01-1812-wheeler-fabric-2914).

street_front_trim.note: K09 dresses none of this front's windows (T-2889): each is named off the photograph (street_front_windows), the arched ones under their voussoirs, and the photograph's stone bands and carved bosses are T-2914's (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

wall_head.note: No cornice (T-2889): the photograph carries the front up into the shaped gable with no eave or cornice across it, and no picture shows the side walls' heads, so they run plain under the 0.05 m eave, as 1625's (L-k01-1812-wheeler-third-storey-2889). Until T-2889 K10's bracketed timber eave stood here, under a 0.45 m overhang the gable had to stand 0.5 m proud of the wall to cover.

roof_form.note: The photograph shows the roof only at the gable's two front corners, a steep slated slope rising behind each shoulder; the roof behind the gable is T-2545's. Built as K01's hip, its street slope behind the gable (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

roof_pitch_deg.note: Steep enough to show at the gable's shoulders as the photograph does, and to stand its ridge (16.7 m) under the gable's apex (17.0 m); the Pennsylvania slate is cut for 45 degrees and steeper (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

eave_overhang_m.note: T-2889: the photograph runs the front straight up into the gable with no eave across it, and shows the side slopes only behind the gable's shoulders, so the eave is plain and almost flush, 0.05 m, as 1625's: the gable's slab, which K01 stands just proud of the street fascia, then stands 0.07 m before the wall below, on the wall's own plane within the rock face's own relief, and keeps the street run of the eave's gutter inside it. No picture shows the side walls' eaves (L-k01-1812-wheeler-third-storey-2889).

stoop_width_m.note: Between the stair's two balustrades the photograph shows treads about 1.7-1.8 m wide.

entrance_bay.note: The photograph puts the arched entrance and its stair at the north end of the front, beside the south projection.

front_bays.note: The two bays' centres along the front from the south wall, through the photograph's camera: the projection's and the large arched window's over it (about 2.5-2.8 m) and the entrance's, the paired window's over it and the small arched window's (6.4-6.5 m).

windows.why_not_ordinary: the basement light under the arched window, read off the photograph: about 1.9 m wide and 1 m high from about 0.1 m over the walk, barred with ironwork; built 0.65 m high on a 0.72 m sill, because K08 keeps a storey's openings clear of its 0.6 m plinth (the light's true height and its scrolls are T-2544's) (T-2543)
the first storey's large round-arched window, read off the photograph: 1.45 m between its jambs, its sill 0.58 m over the floor and its crown about 2.5 m over the sill (T-2543)
the second storey's paired window under its transom, read off the photograph: 2.3 m across the pair (T-2543)

bays.note: The south projection: the photograph shows the south part of the front carried forward through the basement and the first two storeys to a flat top at the third floor, where the balcony stands; it reads 4.75-5.0 m across against (built at 4.75 m, which lands its north face on the photograph's within a few pixels) the sheet's 8.5 m front (the sheet's own step is 3.9 m from the south wall, which the photograph does not bear out, and it is built to the photograph). It stands out 1.2 m, the kit's most against the sheet's 1.3 m, and 0.3 m in from the south corner where the photograph has it flush, because K08 keeps a bay that far from a corner (built otherwise, L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543). Its openings are the photograph's. On its flat top stands the photograph's balcony (T-2888): an iron rail on the eaves, 0.1 m in from their edge, round the cheeks and the front from the wall to the wall, 0.55 m high, its balusters 0.24 m apart. Through the camera the print's rail rises about 47 px (0.51 m at the projection's 92.4 px a metre) over the cornice's top edge, which hides its foot, and its balusters stand about 22 px apart; the posts', rails' and balusters' sections and the inset are K08's to choose, and the print's solid stone panel in the middle of the front run, rising to a central pedestal, is built as more of the iron rail (L-k08-1812-projection-balcony-2888). T-2914: its wall is brick over the basement (brick_above_m 1.65 m, the principal floor), as the print's first and second storeys are, the brick showing round the arched window and either side of the paired one; its plinth, its bands at the two floors, its sills, heads and reveals stay stone. The print's quoined jambs and the band at the arched window's spring are not laid on it (L-k01-1812-wheeler-fabric-2914). T-2915: its dressings are laid as the print's (dress), read at 2x crops of x 280-770, y 780-1380 px at the projection's 92.4 px a metre (the horizon at y 1408, 1.6 m): the paired window's jambs in dressed stones about 37 and 50 px (0.40 and 0.55 m) out from its frame in turn, in courses about 20 px (0.22 m), from its sill to its head, built as ten courses from 6.24 to 8.43 m; the arched window's in taller stones about 40 px (0.43 m), returning about 35-45 and 55-65 px (0.40 and 0.62 m built), four courses from its sill to the band; that band, at y 1140-1175 px (4.12-4.5 m), a long stone running from each corner of the projection to the arch, built at 3.9-4.28 m so its bed stands about 0.1 m under the kit's spring (4.0 m) as the print's under its arch's, 0.04 m proud and stopping at the arch ring's extrados; and under the second storey's jambs, in the band over the second floor's belt, two carved shields about 42-45 px across and 37 px high (0.47 by 0.40 m) centred at y 1012 (5.89 m) and 132 and 139 px (about 1.46 m) either side of the window's axis, built as oval bosses standing for the carving, 0.05 m proud in a moulded ring. The courses' joints, the quoins' 0.02 m and the bosses' carving are the kit's, and the cheeks, which the print does not see, are left plain (L-k01-1812-wheeler-carved-2915).

side_bays.note: No picture shows the side walls; their windows are T-2545's (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

north_bays.note: The north wall stands at the lot line beside 1808: blank.

rear_wings.note: The trace's rear part, behind the main body: 10.6 m deep and narrower by the 1.65 m south strip, carried at the house's three storeys ('3B' covers the whole outline); its windows and flat deck are reconstructed (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

sash_by_storey.note: The contract's sash rows, which K01 lays on walls it is given no picture of; every street window is named off the photograph since T-2889 (street_front_windows), and the main body's side and rear walls are blank or behind the rear range, so no window is laid from them. The values are the photograph's earlier reading: the second storey's pair over the entrance at K01's widest sash, its sill 0.51 m over the floor, and the third storey's arched windows flat-headed (T-2543).

roof_covering.note: The photograph's slopes at the gable's shoulders are laid in small units; slate, as the row's other K01 roofs (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

chimneys.note: The photograph shows one tall corbelled stack over the south wall behind the gable; its place along the wall is reconstructed.

rainwater.note: The photograph shows a downpipe down each end of the front; neither is built on the front yet, because the north one would stand on the eave's corner bracket and the projection stands where the south one comes down (T-2544); the two pipes here run down the south wall, clear of its corner brackets. The gutter is K04's half-round on brackets (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543).

window_kit.note: The street windows from the photograph's kinds (T-2889): the second storey's wide mullioned window under its transom, the third storey's large segmental fanlight window over the balcony and its small round-arched one. The rear range's windows, which no picture shows, keep the paired sash. The street front has no basement light on its main wall (the projection's barred light is K08's), so it names no area light.

entrance_kit.note: The photograph's entrance is a round-arched porch on the north bay over a straight stair: K07's deep round-arched doorway. The porch's own broad arch (about 3.2 m across, its crown about 5.2 m over the walk) and the door's side light under it are the kit's to learn (T-2544).

shaped_gable.note: The front's shaped gable, read through the photograph's camera at the front's 88.5 px a metre about its centre (695 px, v 4.24 m): the outline's half-width and height over the walk at ten points from the kneelers (4.07 m out at 11.63 m) up the swell (its four lower points drawn in 0.15-0.2 m after the first render was laid over the print), the shoulder stone (1.24 m at 15.14 m) and the drawn-in head to the apex block at 17.0 m, the finial over it to about 17.5 m; the grid window 1.64 m across, its sill 13.33 m and its head 14.59 m over the walk. T-2889: its face brought onto the wall's own plane, as the photograph's is: the eave under it is 0.05 m (eave_overhang_m), so the slab stands 0.02 m before the street fascia and 0.07 m before the wall below, and its foot is set at 12.08 m, just over the third storey's two arched windows (crowns at 12.05 and 12.0 m), whose voussoirs run on up its face; the kneelers stand 4.07 m out, where the print's are, on a ledge at 12.55 m, 0.15 m over the street fascia; and it takes the eave's gutter (takes_gutter), as the print shows no gutter across the front: the gutter's street run is not built and its side runs die into the base, which runs out past the side walls to take them. Built otherwise: under the curves the base runs out square to the eave's corners and up to that ledge, where the photograph's outline leaves the wall at the kneelers, about 11.6-11.7 m; the slab is the side walls' brick where the print shows brick dressed in stone (L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543; L-k01-1812-wheeler-third-storey-2889). T-2951: the outline re-read against the print with the render's silhouette laid over it, both sides at a tenth of a metre (the south side reads about 0.25 m wider than the north all the way up, the print's crinkle or a slight roll, so the build takes the mean): the swell 2.98 m out at 13.0 m, 2.43 at 14.0 and 1.83 at 14.5 (built 0.04 m inside each, which the coping's projection gives back in the render), a convex curve swinging in to the shoulder, where the draft stood 0.3-0.5 m wide of it, and the head a bell drawn in from the shoulders (1.10 m at 15.3, 0.92 at 15.75, 0.75 at 16.0, 0.54 at 16.25, 0.35 at 16.5, built 0.05 m inside each) to the finial's square plinth, 0.48 m across from 16.65 m to the apex block at 17.0 m, which the draft drew as a point; the shoulder stones square blocks 0.9-1.62 m out from 14.6 to 15.22 m (the print's south 0.90-1.62 at 14.68-15.3, its north 0.92-1.60 about 0.15 lower), standing over the outline through the slab; the grid window three rows of three lights in the same 1.64 by 1.26 m opening, each light about 0.44 m across between 0.16 m stone mullions and 0.37 m high over a 0.07 m stone transom, one pane each, as the print's dark lights show no bars; and each kneeler a carved scroll console at the front's corner, its roll 0.4 m across from 11.35 m and its body up to a cap under the slab's foot, under a small pinnacle on the ledge 3.85 m out (the print's kneeler stone stands about 3.6-3.95 m out and rises to about 12.85 m). Not built: the window's quoined side stones and the wavy hood over it, the sunk panel in each shoulder stone and the scroll's carving beyond its roll and eye (L-k01-1812-wheeler-gable-2951).

street_front_windows.note: T-2889: the main wall's street windows read off the photograph through its camera (data/reference_views/wheeler_house_1812_prairie/levy_front.json: level and square to the front, 88.5 px a metre at the main front's plane, the walk at y 1549.6 px, v = 3.54 + (x - 633) / 88.5 m from the south wall), each on 2-3x crops of the print. Second storey, over the entrance: one wide window, 1.64 m across its frame (x 818-962 px) on a stone mullion, two plate lights under a stone transom whose foot is about 0.68 m under the head, the transom's lights low over it; its sill at 6.07 m (y 1013) and its head at 8.03 m (y 840), centred at 6.44 m. Third storey, over the balcony: the large window, 2.78 m between its jambs (x 447-693 px), its jambs rising to a spring at 11.30 m (y 550) and its head a flat segmental arch to a crown at 12.05 m (y 483), rising 0.75 m, a fanlight with radial bars over three lights; its foot is hidden behind the balcony and the projection's top, so its sill is set at 9.9 m, the 0.15 m K08 keeps an opening over where the projection's roof meets the wall (9.73 m). Its voussoirs run out about 0.43 m round the head (y 445 px at the crown), fifteen of them, under a keystone carried to 12.76 m (y 420), 0.37 m across its top. To its north the smaller arched window: 1.2 m across (x 840-946 px), a round head springing at about 11.4 m to a crown at 12.0 m (y 488), its sill at 10.75 m (y 598), centred at 6.48 m, in a ring of about eleven voussoirs 0.4 m deep. Built otherwise: the large window's three lights are a K06 three-light sash, where the print's middle light is wider than the two beside it and carries an arched head of its own, and its fanlight has radial bars only, where the print's also has a concentric bar; the small window is glazed as K06's round fanlight sash, where the print shows it filled with a patterned light or panel; the voussoirs are a ring of equal stones standing 0.1 m before the wall, where the print's alternate long and short into the brick; the transom's small squared glazing is not built (L-k01-1812-wheeler-third-storey-2889). T-2914: the second storey's north window in a dressed quoined surround, as the print's: its jambs a stone about 0.17 m and 0.32 m out from the frame in turn (15 and 28 px at 88.5 px a metre, 3x crops of x 760-1060), the long and short read on both jambs, and a lintel course about 0.17 m deep over the head; the stones' heights are the kit's courses, not the print's joints. T-2915: the carved stone over the north window, read at 4x crops of the print (x 760-1000, y 660-850 px) at the main front's 88.5 px a metre, the walk at y 1549.6: from the lintel up, a fillet at y 790-795 (8.53-8.58 m), the carved frieze to y 757 (8.95 m), an interlace of crossing straps and leaves; a moulded band to y 740 (9.15 m); the patterned band to y 697 (9.63 m), rows of small sunk oblong panels about 30-35 px (0.34-0.40 m) long whose joints break row on row; and a ledge to y 683 (9.79 m). Each runs from the projection's north face (x 775 px) to the north corner. So the front's belts are the photograph's: the 5.4-5.6 m belt under the second storey kept, the moulded band 8.95-9.15 m and the ledge 9.63-9.79 m, where K01 had laid its own 9.30-9.45 m belt at the third floor; and two carved belts between them, carved from s 5.05 m (the projection's north face; behind the projection they are belt courses only) to the corner: the frieze 8.55-8.95 m carved with T-2819's guilloche, rings 0.15 m in radius crossing at 1.5 radii, standing for the print's interlace, and the panel band 9.15-9.63 m in two rows of sunk panels about 0.36 m long between raised ribs, each row's joints halfway along the row under it (L-k01-1812-wheeler-carved-2915).

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Wheeler, George H., Residence (1812 S. Prairie Ave.). Albert Levy, Architectural Photographic Series (New York), nos. 31, 33; photograph of the street front, c. 1885-1900. Ryerson & Burnham Art and Architecture Archives, Art Institute of Chicago, Special 779.4 L66a no. 31, 33.
what_it_supplies: the front's storey heights, the raised basement and the stair's rise, read at the front's plane
the south projection's width and height and its windows
the entrance's place on the north and the openings' places and sizes
the shaped gable's outline, its grid window and finial
what_it_does_not_supply: colour: the print is monochrome, so every stone, brick and paint colour stays reconstructed
the side and rear walls, and the roof behind the gable except its two front corners
depth: how far the projection stands out is the 1911 sheet's

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2329) in place under the same id by T-2543, piece 1 of T-1884: K01 frontage kit, built from Albert Levy's photograph (levy_1812_prairie_photo, camera data/reference_views/wheeler_house_1812_prairie/levy_front.json) on the 1911 sheet's plan (s28fp-1812-b1). What the kit cannot yet build as the photograph shows is listed in the camera's match record and is T-2544's and T-2545's; every invention is L-k01-1812-wheeler-front-2543.
